chunks: "Whoever breaks a fast for one day of the Month of Ramadan, the spirit of faith departs from him. And whoever intentionally breaks the fast in the Month of Ramadan, upon him is one kaffarah and the making up of one day in its place; and how can he have the like of it?"

As for the report that has been narrated regarding one who intentionally breaks the fast for a day in the Month of Ramadan, that three kaffarahs are upon him, then I give fatwa according to it concerning one who breaks the fast through intercourse forbidden to him or through food forbidden to him, due to the presence of that in the narrations of Abi al-Husayn al-Asadi — may Allah be pleased with him — in what came to him from al-Shaykh Abi Ja'far Muhammad ibn 'Uthman al-'Umari — may Allah sanctify his soul.

key_terms.رُوحُ الْإِيمَانِ: the spirit of faith, indicating severe spiritual loss
key_terms.شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: the Month of Ramadan, the obligatory month of sawm
key_terms.قَضَاءُ يَوْمٍ: making up one missed day of fasting
key_terms.كَفَّارَةٌ: expiation required for violating the fast

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on intentionally breaking a fast in the Month of Ramadan?
ai.summary: This hadith states that deliberately breaking the fast in Ramadan is a grave act with both spiritual and legal consequences. It establishes one kaffarah and one make-up fast as the basic ruling, while the appended ruling applies three kaffarahs in cases where the fast was broken through something haram such as forbidden intercourse or forbidden food.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1892 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"Whoever breaks a fast during the Month of Ramadan, the spirit of faith departs from him. Whoever intentionally breaks a fast in the month of Ramadan must offer one expiation and make up a day in its place. But how can he ever truly replace it?"
